commands.label: Parse the exact Android.bp through Blueprint and emit a Ninja manifest
Execute the generated build rule through Ninja

go.mod.content_utf8:
module corpuscheck

go 1.25
require github.com/google/blueprint v0.0.0
replace github.com/google/blueprint => ./blueprint

observed_ninja:
# ******************************************************************************
# ***            This file is generated and should not be edited             ***
# ******************************************************************************
#
# This file contains variables, rules, and pools with name prefixes indicating
# they were generated by the following Go packages:
#
#     corpuscheck [from Go package corpuscheck]
#
ninja_required_version = 1.7.0

rule g.corpuscheck.genrule
    command = ${cmd}

# # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # # #
# Module:  corpus_hello_world
# Variant:
# Type:    genrule
# Factory: main.main.func1
# Defined: Android.bp:1:1

build hello.txt: g.corpuscheck.genrule
    cmd = printf 'Hello, World!\n' > hello.txt
default hello.txt
toolchain: AOSP Blueprint with a minimal genrule module fixture and Ninja 1.11.1
reproduction_command: go run . Android.bp && ninja -f build.ninja hello.txt && cat hello.txt
semantic_scope: The upstream Blueprint engine loaded the original Android.bp, instantiated its module, and emitted a real Ninja build. The test host provides the subset of genrule that binds the declared out and cmd properties. Ninja ran the command and created the greeting file.
path_normalization: Temporary paths use stable placeholders. Source hashes refer to the repository files listed in artifact_sha256.
